main_text.p: 1.3 §.9. D. de vi & vi armat.Neque obstat 3. Quod jure expressum sit, eum qui armis venit, nos posse armis repellere; adeoque à contrario sensu procedat, eum qui sine armis venit, etiam sine armis esse repellendum. Respondeo enim 1. Argumentum à contrario sensu in jure non semper procedere, præsertim si textus alii juris obstent, qui aliquid asserunt contra sensum contrarium. Wesemb. bec[?] con. sil.[?] 19. num. 17.2. Is etiam qui pugno nos adoritur, si robustus sit, sic ut vel pugno hominem necaverit, merito dicitur armis nos aggredi, saltem iis instrumentis quæ sunt vice armorum, cum ipse iis æquè atque alii armis nocere possit.
Neque aliud suadent Theologicæ rationes, quibus eo quo dictum est modo, quisque se tueri poterit. Licet enim malum nobis illatum avertere,

page.notes: Left-margin notes: the first is "1.3 §.9. D. de vi & vi armat." (the "1.3" may be "L.3" or "I.3"). The second is "Wesemb. bec con. sil. 19. num. 17.": "bec" is probably "hic" and "sil." is probably "fil." or "sil."; both are marked [?]. The "3" after "obstat" and the numerals "1." and "2." are printed section numbers and kept as printed. The word "malum" at the foot of the text is set in heavier type than its neighbours; it is copied as plain text. The final word "etiam" stands alone at the right below the last line and is treated as the catchword.
